 Monza, another defeat: they advance, allow a comeback, and then fail to equalize on a penalty. Bologna celebrates.
 In a match featuring three penalties, the Biancorossi broke the deadlock with Varela's usual strike, but then struggled to build and ended up losing. Cutrone missed an equalizer from the spot, and the standings now look more challenging.
 di ALESSANDRO STELLA October 31, 2026 Cutrone has a penalty saved by Skorupski, Monza KO
 Facebook X WhatsApp Print October 31, 2026 – The more conservative approach , visibly and inevitably after conceding so many goals, doesn't pay off . Monza lets Bologna come from behind , fails to break the away taboo, and falls for the third consecutive time. Varela's ninth goal in his first nine Serie A games from the penalty spot was in vain (the last Under 22 to do so in Serie A history was Pierino Prati in 1968): Pobega and Bernardeschi, also from the spot, give the Emilians of former coach Palladino a third consecutive 2-1 victory.
 However, what weighs heavily on the Brianza team, in addition to yet another defensive blunder (by Lucchesi this time), is Cutrone's missed penalty, which would likely have been worth at least a point . Instead, the number 10 continues his difficult personal situation, and the team's standings remain stagnant, with the relegation zone creeping ever closer .
 Overall, it was a poor performance for Juric's team, who, aside from their two penalty kicks, created virtually nothing except two missed chances at the end. The coach had made it clear that a more cautious style would have led to the team losing their attacking brilliance, but it's clear that finding a balance is urgent .
 Juric's choices
 Monza's formation remains the same, with a few differences from Napoli. Koaudio returns to defense after recent injury issues, with Goglichidze and Lucchesi confirmed alongside him. Colombo and Foe-Ondoa have another chance in midfield , while Birindelli returns to his traditional role on the right.
 Up front, alongside the untouchable Varela, are Dany Mota (rested against the Azzurri) and, somewhat surprisingly, Zeballos, who until today had only been a starter in the away match in Rome.
 First half: Varela breaks the deadlock from the penalty spot
 The match heated up immediately, and within seconds, Rossoblu's Odgaard threatened with a header. Seconds later, Zeballos broke free on the counterattack , skipping past an opponent and attempting a shot. The ball was deflected, but the rebound found Dany Mota, who beat Theate to the ball and placed it in the box. The penalty was confirmed by VAR and converted by the usual, unstoppable Varela: Monza took the lead .
 The pace remained high, with both teams man-marking and pushing hard down the flanks. Zeballos missed the winner from Mota's cross. Bologna came close to equalizing in the 15th minute: Foe-Ondoa , like in Turin, lost a dangerous ball near his own penalty area, but this time Tornqvist miraculously denied Pobega . Mangas also proved invaluable in stopping Bernardeschi's rebound.
 Pobega scored a great goal, it's 1-1
 Not just quality but also a lot of competitive spirit, which slowly made the game rather dirty, fragmented and full of fouls that led to three yellow cards in the first 21 minutes . Just when it seemed to have reached a stalemate, the Emilians equalized : in the 33rd minute, Miranda took a beautiful corner (given by Kouadio) and found Pobega who, unmarked, was able to send the ball into the net with a powerful low volley . The half ended without any real further chances, but Bologna now seemed to be in control of the match.
 Second half: Bernardeschi turns the tables, Cutrone misses the equaliser
 In the second half, Juric made an immediate substitution: Zeballos, who had fallen off, was replaced by Robinson. However, the Englishman struggled to get into the game, and Monza's general suffering continued. Juric's men were unable to get out of their own half, and in the 10th minute, Lucchesi brought down Theate in the box from a corner: after a VAR review , Zanotti awarded the second penalty of the day. Bernardeschi beat Tornqvist from eleven meters to make it 2-1 .
 The Brianza-born coach attempts to respond with further substitutions: Mout comes in, and most importantly, Idrissa Touré, making his Monza debut after several injury problems. The German begins his adventure as a winger. There's also a revolution up front: Dany Mota and Varela, penalty aside, are out, completely nullified by the defenders for the first time, and Ngonge and Cutrone come on .
 And it was the latter who had a sensational chance to equalize and redeem himself after falling back in the pecking order. In the 36th minute, Robinson fired up and sent in a cross that Zortea handled . Another VAR review, another penalty. Cutrone stepped up to the spot, but this time Skorupski stretched well and saved Bologna .

 Bologna (3-4-2-1) : Skorupski 7,5; Vitik 6,5 (29' st Darmian sv), Casale 6,5, Theate 5,5; Zortea 5,5 (37' st Amondarain sv), Ferguson 6,5, Pobega 7 (29' st El Azzouzi sv), Miranda 6,5; Bernardeschi 6,5 (37' st Dobvik sv), Odgaard 5,5 (19' st Mbangula 6); Cambiaghi 6,5. Annex Palladino 7.
 Monza (3-4-2-1) : Törnqvist 6,5; Kouadio 5 (20' st Touré 5,5), Lucchesi 5, Goglichidze 5,5; Birindelli 6, Foe Ondoa 5,5, Colombo 5,5 (20' st Mout 6), Mangas 5; Dany Mota 6 (26' st Ngonge 5,5), Zeballos 6 (1' st Robinson 6); Varela 6,5 (26' st Cutrone 5). All. Juric 5,5.
 Referee: Zanotti from Rimini 6.
